extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and graduate students studying Ricci flow, geometric analysis, and 3-manifold topology
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and technical conditions for constructing and estimating Ricci flows with δ-cutoff surgeries on compact normalized 3-manifolds (Perelman-style surgery). Includes canonical neighborhood assumptions, surgery localization, curvature/volume hypotheses and resulting noncollapsing and canonical-neighborhood conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (accuracy ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: The canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy parameter ε: points with sufficiently large scalar curvature have neighborhoods which are either ε-necks or ε-caps (with associated constants C1(ε), C2(ε) appearing in the assumption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used throughout to classify local geometry of high-curvature points. The text uses this assumption to deduce that neighborhoods are (strong) ε-necks or 3/4 ε-caps, to apply Lemma 7.3.5, and to enforce κ-noncollapsing. One must choose C1(ε) large enough (e.g., larger than constants from lemmas invoked).

rubrics_metrics.name: δ-cutoff surgery localization (surgeries occur deep in ε-horns)
rubrics_metrics.description: δ-cutoff surgeries are performed at points lying deeply in ε-horns; the surgery uses a cutoff radius h(t) (the 'cutoff radius at the time') and the gluing cap and adjacent δ-neck structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surgery points are taken deep inside ε-horns so that the adjacent δ-neck approximates an ancient κ-solution; surgeries remove caps/glued regions and leave the remainder approximated by standard solutions. This localization ensures the canonical neighborhood assumption remains valid after surgery and that surgery times cannot accumulate (because each surgery decreases volume by at least h^3(t_i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-time existence structure (functions δ(t) and r(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist nonincreasing continuous positive functions δ(t) and r(t) on [0, ∞) (with δ(t) ≤ ¯δ(t) etc.) such that, for any normalized compact orientable three-manifold initial data and any positive δ(t) < given bound, the Ricci flow with δ-cutoff surgeries exists with the pinching and canonical neighborhood assumptions satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 7.4.3: under appropriate choice of δ(t) and r(t) the flow with surgery either becomes extinct in finite time (finite number of surgeries) or exists for all time with at most finitely many surgeries in each finite time interval. δ(t) and r(t) must be chosen (nonincreasing) small enough to guarantee the hypotheses of the canonical neighborhood and pinching assumptions at each surgery time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery volume-decrease and non-accumulation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Each δ-cutoff surgery cuts down the volume by at least an amount h^3(t_i) with h(t_i) depending only on δ(t_i) and r(t_i); combined with the evolution inequality for the minimum scalar curvature, this implies surgery times cannot accumulate in finite time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fact that surgeries reduce volume by a definite amount (h^3) and that R_min(t) is nondecreasing; volume satisfies an upper-derivative inequality (V'(t) ≤ −(2/3) R_min(t) V(t) in the flow) leading to a global bound on volume decrease and precluding accumulation of surgery times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preconditions for local curvature/compactness conclusions (parabolic neighborhood hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply the curvature / noncollapsing / canonical-neighborhood conclusions one assumes the solution (with surgeries) is defined on the whole parabolic neighborhood P(x0, t0, r0, 2 r0^2), satisfies |Rm| ≤ r0^{-2} there, and Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0, r0)) ≥ A^{-1} r0^3 (for given A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core hypotheses of Theorem 7.5.1: existence on the specified parabolic neighborhood, a curvature upper bound on that parabolic cylinder, and a volume lower bound at time t0. Also require δ(t) in the relevant time interval be ≤ ¯δ_A(t0) as in the theorem statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-noncollapsing conclusion (Theorem 7.5.1(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the parabolic neighborhood, curvature and volume hypotheses there exists κ = κ(A, ε) > 0 so that the solution is κ-noncollapsed on all scales less than r0 in the ball B_{t0}(x0, A r0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: κ depends only on A and ε (and constants in canonical neighborhood assumption). To guarantee this, one must ensure each δ-cutoff in the relevant time interval is sufficiently small (δ ≤ ¯δ_A(t0)) so admissible curve/L-length estimates apply and prevent collapse. The proof uses admissible/barely admissible curves and Perelman-type reduced-length estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curvature threshold implies canonical neighborhood (Theorem 7.5.1(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists K1 = K1(A, ε) such that any point x ∈ B_{t0}(x0, A r0) with scalar curvature R(x,t0) ≥ K1 r0^{-2} has a canonical neighborhood B_{t0}(x, σ) (with B_{t0}(x, σ) ⊂ B_{t0}(x, 2σ)) which is either a strong ε-neck or an ε-cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K1 depends on A and ε and comes from the canonical neighborhood assumption together with the local curvature/volume hypotheses. This gives a quantitative threshold for 'high curvature' which forces standard (neck/cap) geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-scale curvature upper bound (Theorem 7.5.1(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If r0 ≤ ¯r sqrt(t0) for some ¯r = ¯r(A, ε) then there is K2 = K2(A, ε) with R ≤ K2 r0^{-2} on B_{t0}(x0, A r0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This part gives a uniform upper curvature bound on the larger ball under a smallness condition relating r0 and t0 (scale vs. time). Constants ¯r and K2 depend only on A and ε. This prevents unexpected blow-up at those scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissible / barely admissible curve L-length estimate for surgery control (7.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any barely admissible space-time curve γ (one that stays in the unaﬀected region except possibly touching the surgery boundary) parametrized by t with γ(t0)=x, there is a lower bound of the form ∫_{t_γ}^{t0} (R(γ(t),t) + |γ̇(t)|^2) dt ≥ L r0 for arbitrarily large L (once δ is chosen sufficiently small depending on L, t0, r(t0), ε).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This estimate (7.5.1) is used to rule out collapsing near surgeries and to apply reduced-length arguments. To make it hold one must choose each δ-cutoff in the relevant time interval smaller than some ¯δ(L, t0, r(t0), ε). It is central to establishing κ-noncollapsing in the surgically modified setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of positive sectional-curvature components in surgery procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The surgery procedure removes every connected component which has positive sectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step is part of the surgery construction to maintain the canonical neighborhood / pinching assumptions afterward. Removing such components simplifies topology (they are spherical) and helps to control geometry and volume in subsequent estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching assumption (preserved through surgery)
rubrics_metrics.description: A curvature pinching assumption (Perelman-type) is maintained throughout the evolution and surgeries; it is a standing hypothesis used to control the behavior of the flow and to choose parameters like θ in curvature estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinching is used repeatedly (e.g., to compare scalar curvatures, to choose θ = D'/2(D' + C(B+...)), and to ensure approximations by the standard solution). One must check pinching is preserved and holds at surgery times for subsequent canonical-neighborhood arguments.
